issues.description: Method ExcellenceLand.isExcellentEnough: The problem statement / UML require a boolean getter for the attribute 'excellentEnough' (a no-argument method, e.g. public boolean isExcellentEnough()). The solution implementation provides public boolean isExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck) — i.e. the method takes a boolean parameter. This parameter mismatch means tests or student implementations expecting a standard no-argument getter will fail to find the correct method and may not compile or pass tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a standard no-argument getter in ExcellenceLand that returns the excellentEnough field (public boolean isExcellentEnough()). Remove the unexpected boolean parameter from the existing isExcellentEnough method or add an overloaded no-argument isExcellentEnough() that returns the field. This will align the implementation with the UML/problem specification and with tests that expect a no-argument getter.

issues.description: The UML/problem declares a boolean attribute named 'excellentEnough' in ExcellenceLand and requires public getters for all attributes (implying a standard no-argument getter, e.g. isExcellentEnough()). In the solution implementation, the method is declared as public boolean isExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck) (a single-parameter method). Because it has a parameter, it is not the conventional zero-argument getter for the 'excellentEnough' attribute. Students implementing the required getter or automated tests expecting a no-argument getter will be confused or blocked by this mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a standard no-argument getter that returns the boolean field, e.g. public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; }. If additional behavior requiring a parameter is desired, add a separate method with a distinct name (or overload with different semantics) but keep the zero-argument getter to match the UML/problem requirements.
